claim: For every nonconstant smooth periodic profile \(g\) on \(\mathbb T\), the formal cosine-drive Floquet correction \(\frac{\epsilon^2}{4\omega^2}[B_g,[A,B_g]]\), with \(A=-\partial_x^2\) and \(B_g=-2g'\partial_x-g''\), has principal coefficient \(a_2(x)=8(2(g''(x))^2-g'(x)g'''(x))\) that is not identically zero; \(a_2\equiv0\) holds only when \(g\) is constant. Since the moment term \(C_g=-(g')^2\) is multiplication-only, the moment-averaged operator is not the complete formal Floquet expansion for any nonconstant smooth periodic profile; the result does not assert convergence of the full unbounded-operator series.

scientific_limitations_and_integrity.integrity: The nonzero coefficient is derived algebraically; the high-frequency expansion is explicitly treated as formal under the stated scope.
limits: No convergence of the full Magnus or van Vleck series is claimed.
No operator-norm or propagator-level remainder estimate is claimed for the unbounded, potentially non-self-adjoint generator.
The classification is limited to one-dimensional smooth periodic profiles and the principal coefficient at the stated formal order.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.scope: Exact differential-operator identity classifying when the principal coefficient of the formal order-epsilon-squared, inverse-frequency-squared correction can vanish for smooth periodic profiles.

title: A nonzero Floquet correction for a curved-space drive
